title: Asalha, the fifth time
hook: the first sermon, and the rains retreat ahead
tomorrow: who comes back to the old house once a year?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Vesak for the fifth time: birth, awakening and passing on one full moon, and a lamp for each year on this path. Five years of lamps. Now the next full moon, and the rain behind it.
screen: `FIVE YEARS OF LAMPS.` → `THE NEXT FULL MOON.`

segments.voice: Rain on the windshield, a storm alert on the phone, plans quietly canceled: some seasons tell everyone to stay in. In the Buddha's India, the monsoon did that to the roads. His monks kept walking anyway. And the neighbors started grumbling. The Vinaya, the monks' rulebook, keeps their complaint: these monks tramp around in the rains, crushing green shoots and the small creatures in them. Even the birds, people said, build nests in the treetops and stay put. The complaint reached the Buddha, a teacher who walked from town to town himself. What would he do with it?
screen: `THE STORM ALERT. STAY IN.` → `THE MONKS KEEP WALKING.` → `EVEN THE BIRDS STAY PUT.` → `WHAT WILL HE DO?`

segments.voice: He listened. He told the monks to stay in one place for the rains. That's vassa, the rains retreat, and the Vinaya starts it the day after the Asalha full moon, the night tradition remembers as the first sermon. The rule came years after the sermon, but the calendar sets the two side by side. On the full moon, the wheel is set rolling: at the Deer Park, the Buddha teaches his five old companions about suffering, its cause, its ending and the path. In the sutta a cry goes up from the earth to the heavens: the wheel has been set rolling, and no one in the world can turn it back. Then, on the calendar, the next morning, the walking stops. One way to read that pairing: the teaching wasn't kept by rushing everywhere. It was kept by monks who stopped, stayed in one place through the wet months, and practiced. Monks in Theravada monasteries still keep the rains in one place, and some lay people choose a practice for the season: the precepts on holy days, a drink given up, an extra morning at the temple. The odd part to pass on tonight: the rains retreat began with neighbors upset about trampled plants. Five Asalhas on this path, and the sermon still starts again each year, with someone choosing to sit still and look.
screen: `STAY IN ONE PLACE FOR THE RAINS.` · `THE WHEEL SET ROLLING AT THE DEER PARK.` · `THE WALKING STOPS, THE PRACTICE STAYS.` · `A PRACTICE FOR THE SEASON.` · then, large: `THE WHEEL STILL TURNS.`

segments.voice: Choose one practice for the rains, the season ahead: small enough to keep on an ordinary Tuesday. Name what you hope it gives you, the one thing most likely to get in its way, and what you'll do when that happens. Then sit with your choice, settled, like a monk who has stopped walking.
Asalha: the full moon of the first sermon, and the night before the rains retreat begins.
Carry this: the wheel still turns, each time someone stays put long enough to see. Two of seven in the festival year.

Asalha.meaning: a full-moon month; its full moon remembers the first sermon

Vinaya.meaning: the rulebook for Buddhist monks and nuns

vassa.meaning: the rains retreat, when monks stay in one place

Deer Park.meaning: the park where the Buddha gave his first sermon

sources.ref: Vinaya, Mahavagga III.1 (the rains residence: the lay people's complaint, the allowance to stay put)
Samyutta Nikaya 56.11 (Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta: the first sermon, Kondañña's insight, the cry through the heavens)

notes: Mahavagga III.1 paraphrased: people complain that the Sakyan monks walk on tour in the rains, trampling green grass and harming small living things, while even other ascetics, and birds that make nests in the treetops, stay put; the Buddha then allows the rains residence. Some translations render the birds as vultures; voiced simply as 'birds'. Confirm.
The rains residence beginning 'the day after the Asalha full moon' is the Vinaya's earlier start date (there is also a later one); voiced as the Vinaya starting it there. Confirm.
SN 56.11 paraphrased: addressed to the group of five; the devas' cry that the wheel cannot be stopped by anyone in the world. Kondañña's insight is left out here (told on day 1762). Confirm.
Lay rains practices given as examples with 'some lay people'; confirm they're fair. 'Monks in Theravada monasteries still keep the rains in one place' — confirm wording.
Original: आषाढ is the Sanskrit month name (Pali Āsāḷha); confirm the say-it line.

Shape: story (the neighbors' complaint, told as an episode; the teach answers what the Buddha did).
